authority_rule: This file is the sole authoritative project-management decision source. Other docs/data may describe implementation details but must not override requirements, priorities, decisions, conflicts, active gate, or quality status recorded here.

target_profile.quality: Balanced Medium / selective High where visually important
target_profile.visual_quality_rule: The supported low-spec profile must still look intentional, attractive and game-ready. Preserve higher perceived quality for hero characters, nearby architecture, terrain readability, key materials and primary lighting; recover performance first from distant shadows, far-detail density, nonessential effects, LOD/cull distance and other lower-salience costs. Do not globally flatten the game to Low merely to meet the frame target.

product_north_star: Let the player live the Peter Jackson film story as a playable adventure rather than inventing a replacement main story.
Make the world feel alive, beautiful, explorable and responsive while preserving story chronology and low-spec performance.
Preserve every meaningful user request and decision so chat loss or developer changes never erase project intent.
Prefer player enjoyment, clarity, stable traversal, save continuity and reliable performance over uncontrolled feature quantity.

Deliver a visually strong, enjoyable image on the target laptop through selective quality budgeting rather than uniformly low settings; performance optimization must preserve the player's sense of beauty, atmosphere and authored world quality.
operating_rules: Global project-management changes go through the single Governor and a validation branch/PR; workers must not create competing authority files.
One governor, one decision authority. No secondary file may independently redefine requirement status, priority, conflict resolution, active gate, or region acceptance.

Only requests that materially change product scope, story/canon, architecture, acceptance gates, production priority, or external dependency require a stable requirement ID; status questions, clarifications, evidence refreshes, routine CI bookkeeping and implementation notes do not create new requirements.
New requests never silently delete older requests; contradictions become explicit conflicts/decisions here.
The film story spine, build/save/story integrity, target-device performance and required traversal cannot be silently traded away.

Before changing or adding any FILM_CORE beat, verify the exact scene order, participating characters and outcome against the supplied film/script source; do not rely on memory when the source can be checked.
A feature is never called accepted from compile/static evidence alone.

If a previously passed critical gate fails, quarantine the affected acceptance/merge path, repair the smallest failing layer, and rerun the exact failed gate while unrelated safe production work continues.

Permanent root-cause rule: patching over symptoms is not an accepted closure. Every reproducible defect must be reduced to the causal layer, repaired at that layer, guarded against regression where practical, and revalidated at the exact failed gate. Temporary containment may only protect data/branches/runners while the root repair is underway and may not be presented as the solution.
Human pacing and visual review are mandatory for enjoyment/acceptance; CI cannot infer fun.
Developer-owned automation should reproduce and verify defects before asking the owner to spend play time on technical regression checks; never relabel machine checks as visual or pacing approval.

Validation harness semantics are first-class: repeated log copies must not inflate defect counts, save tests must prove disk roundtrip, and every failing debt gate must print concrete asset/package identities.
After W00 machine repair closure, do not delay W01 for invented repair work. Only concrete regression evidence may reopen architectural/root repair.
Final W00 automation must prove packaged runtime data and packaged executable startup before W01 opens.

Do not repeat an expensive UE4 build/cook/package gate merely because an immediate metadata parent was cancelled; reuse the nearest still-valid green proof only across an explicitly safe governance/docs-only ancestry, and fail closed if any runtime/asset/config/packaging path intervenes.

Local tracked launch controllers must never update themselves in place. Any helper that performs git pull while running must execute from an immutable temporary copy and preserve the explicit develop lane.

The programmer handoff must remain branch-simple: develop is canonical development/integration, main is stable/release, and temporary implementation branches self-clean after merge once meaningful content is integrated.
Temporary branches must merge meaningful completed work into develop immediately, then delete the branch ref; only active work or unresolved unique-content salvage may remain outside develop.

Parallel source/PDF/warehouse/asset-preparation lanes may advance without repeating engine gates for administrative-only changes; promotion into runtime remains serialized and technical safety/performance/runtime-data gates stay fail-closed.

Permanent branch closeout invariant: every completed temporary branch is exact-head validated, merged into develop immediately, and its remote ref is deleted after merge so develop never lags completed work. Only an active PR head or a branch with verified unique unsalvaged commits may remain temporarily.
Maximum Safe Production is the default for all eligible project production work even when the owner does not explicitly say 'start chapter' or repeat the throughput instruction.

Story scope is experience-first, not summary-first: the Timeline organizes sequence but never caps detail; compatible Tolkien book-only events/details should be playable when safe, and meaningful discovered source material may not be silently omitted.

Closing a temporary PR is an explicit branch-lifecycle disposition. If it closes unmerged, any useful unique work must first be selectively salvaged into the current authority or recorded by exact commit SHA/disposition; after closure the unchanged remote head ref is deleted. A moved ref or active PR head is preserved as new work.

An active runtime chapter is one owner-facing One-Shot Mega Chapter Finish: preflight the complete chapter payload first, then continue through all required character/world/gameplay/audio/save/performance/acceptance lanes without asking the owner to re-authorize routine internal steps. Internal runtime-changing dependencies may remain serialized for safety; this never permits opening the next runtime chapter early.

hard_invariants.description: Meaningful user requirements and decisions must be persisted in repository data; chat history is never the sole source of truth.
Peter Jackson film continuity remains the primary story spine unless the user explicitly records a product-direction override.
A change must not knowingly introduce build failure, crash, save corruption, story deadlock or route-state loss.
Intended playable routes and required story anchors must not be accepted while blocked, trapping the player, or unreachable.
Features must remain compatible with the target laptop profile: Windows DX11, 720p, Low/Medium, 30 FPS floor target, 8 GB RAM, roughly 2 GB VRAM-class GPU.
Static/compile success must never be presented as PIE, device, performance, pacing or visual acceptance.

A runtime defect is never called fixed from source inspection or static validation alone. Identify the root cause, add a regression signal where feasible, pass exact-head machine gates, then require defect-specific PIE/device observation before closure.

Patching over symptoms is never accepted as defect closure. Every reproducible failure must be traced to its root cause and repaired at the causal layer; temporary containment is allowed only to protect the project while that repair is in progress, and exact-gate revalidation plus a regression guard where practical are required before closure.

The player must not receive gravity in chapter coordinates until the destination world is committed and blocking ground is confirmed. Startup and chapter audits fail closed when grounding cannot be proven.
Heavy production asset growth must follow soft/asynchronous chapter or region ownership; residual synchronous loading is debt to reduce, not a pattern to expand.
High-count non-story decorative detail uses HISM/ISM plus bounded culling where practical; do not multiply independent actors/ticks for foliage or repeated micro-detail.
Per-frame Tick is reserved for bounded time-sensitive behavior. Heavy loading, JSON/file I/O, or unbounded actor/world scans may not be introduced into Tick.
Baked, stationary, CSM and distance-field lighting/shadow choices are measured per scene/profile on the target laptop; no technique is globally declared cheaper without evidence.

Warehouse acquisition/cataloguing must not wait for UE runtime/PIE/device gates. Assets may be DISCOVERED/CANDIDATE/STAGED in bulk, but no file may be promoted to READY_FOR_IMPORT without intake validation (integrity, format, scale/unit, topology/UV/skeleton/texture sanity as applicable, provenance/metadata, and malware/archive hygiene). INTEGRATED and ACCEPTED states still require the relevant UE4.27 build/import/runtime/visual/audio/device evidence.

Expensive Unreal/package evidence is reused only across an explicit safe ancestry. Cancelled metadata parents do not force a recook when a nearby green ancestor remains valid, but any runtime/asset/config/streaming/packaging/unclassified delta breaks inheritance and requires the appropriate fresh lane.

develop is the sole canonical development/programmer-handoff branch and main is stable/release. Temporary branches are short-lived and removed after merge; stale diverged branches are never bulk-merged as a substitute for selective salvage.

The UE4.27 self-hosted GitHub runner must execute only under the proven interactive Windows user through the ShireJourney-GitHubRunner-Watchdog Scheduled Task. Legacy actions.runner.* Windows service registration is not an alternate execution path: it must be absent, or at minimum Stopped+Disabled while pending deletion. NETWORK SERVICE, LOCAL SERVICE and SYSTEM are forbidden. The watchdog continuously removes service-mode ownership and a worker/AI session may not change runner topology without explicit owner authorization.

Once the owner starts a runtime chapter, that chapter is the owner-facing production unit from full preflight through Gate 6/7. Prepare and validate the whole chapter payload before mass promotion; quarantine independent source/provider failures instead of stopping unrelated lanes; keep exactly one runtime-changing integration authority; do not fragment the chapter into owner-facing micro-waves or repeated micro-approval.

conflict_rules: A new request never silently deletes or rewrites an older requirement.
If two active requirements conflict, the conflict must be explicitly recorded and resolved before either can be treated as fully accepted.
Hard invariants cannot be silently overridden by implementation convenience.
A user may explicitly change product direction; that override must be recorded as a decision and linked to affected requirements.
When no explicit user override exists, prefer preserving story/progress integrity and target-device playability over visual scope or feature quantity.
Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the request without destabilizing already validated behavior.

decisions.title: Film story anchors versus player exploration freedom
decisions.resolution: Major film chronology/outcomes remain fixed; exploration, side routes, optional conversations and living-world activity belong primarily between required story anchors.
decisions.rationale: Preserves the user's goal of living the film while allowing meaningful adventure and discovery.

decisions.title: Living-world richness versus target-laptop performance
decisions.resolution: Use rich near-player simulation and cheaper distance-adaptive/offscreen simulation; do not require always-on expensive AI for ambient life.
decisions.rationale: The world should feel alive without sacrificing the low-spec device target.

decisions.title: Source reorganization versus current functional validation gate
decisions.resolution: Define and guard the target Public/Private source architecture now, but perform the physical move as a dedicated maintenance pass after the current F9/F8/chapter/device functional gate is healthy.
decisions.rationale: Preserves organization without mixing a large path/include refactor into unresolved gameplay validation.

decisions.title: Begin a bounded visible character-production pass before the full functional hard gate is manually closed
decisions.resolution: Proceed with a small reversible Frodo/Gandalf visual-motion pass now because the user explicitly wants the game to start feeling playable. Do not change story/save architecture or add a large new subsystem; require static and UE4.27.2 build validation, then return to PIE/device gate evidence.
decisions.rationale: This satisfies the user's explicit current direction while limiting regression risk and preserving the existing hard-gate discipline.

decisions.title: Expand visible character production from player avatars to the full Part I core cast
decisions.resolution: Populate each Part I chapter with its required named cast and regional inhabitants now, while keeping expensive simulation near-player only and preserving film chronology. Use distinct proxies where dedicated production assets do not yet exist, and track those proxies as unfinished rather than pretending the cast is visually complete.
decisions.rationale: The user explicitly wants the world to start feeling inhabited and playable now; chapter-appropriate cast presence gives immediate experiential value without waiting for every final character asset.

decisions.title: Build first in larger batches, then perform a dedicated integration/playtest repair pass
decisions.resolution: Continue substantial character/world/runtime construction now while requiring Pre-Unreal and real UE4.27.2 compile/import gates for each merged batch. Defer detailed PIE, device, pacing and visual acceptance into a later dedicated integration/playtest/repair pass instead of stopping after every small visible feature.
decisions.rationale: The user explicitly wants to see a much more complete game when returning to the laptop and prefers building a larger playable body of work before manual testing.

decisions.title: Freeze after CP54 for real current-head PIE/device verification
decisions.resolution: Stop new checkpoints/content expansion after CP54. Verify the exact develop head in UE4.27 PIE chapter-by-chapter, beginning with Shire; repair blocking failures immediately; log non-blocking ideas only. Defer formal rights-holder outreach and resume material/world enrichment only after the baseline audit is complete.
decisions.rationale: Compile, import and headless startup are green, but the repository itself still records current-head traversal, performance, pacing and visual gates as untested for most chapters. Continuing to stack content would increase regression risk.

decisions.title: Lift the post-CP54 verification freeze and resume construction
decisions.resolution: Treat the post-CP54 verification pass as human-completed on the current validated develop baseline and resume large, guarded game-construction batches. Preserve Pre-Unreal and real UE4.27 build/import regression gates and continue to distinguish implementation from later visual/performance acceptance.
decisions.rationale: The project owner explicitly confirmed that the planned verification/check/fix pass was completed and instructed the project to resume game construction and expansion.

decisions.title: Use the film chronology as the hard spine and expand playable life between anchors
decisions.resolution: For Part I, preserve Peter Jackson film chronology/outcomes as the non-negotiable main route. Expand Shire friendship, party life, companion banter, regional social texture, exploration and environmental storytelling in the spaces between those anchors. Prefer Extended Edition enrichment when compatible, but write original game dialogue and keep optional activity non-blocking.
decisions.rationale: The project owner explicitly wants to feel present inside the film moment-to-moment while also having room to play, explore and enjoy the world.

decisions.title: Living NPC architecture is offline-only, local-first and bounded
decisions.resolution: Implement NPC identity, memory, schedules, goals, needs, emotions, relationships and knowledge limits entirely in local deterministic project systems. If a language model is later added, it must run locally/on-device and remain optional behind strict context/performance guards. Remote/cloud LLM, STT and TTS calls are not part of the shipped gameplay architecture.
decisions.rationale: The project owner explicitly clarified that the game is offline. This also avoids API keys, internet dependency, recurring service cost, cloud outages and uncontrolled latency while protecting the 8 GB / ~2 GB VRAM target.

decisions.title: Shipped game AI must work with the internet disconnected
decisions.resolution: Treat offline execution as a hard product constraint. NPC intelligence, memory, relationships, schedules, goals, emotions, dialogue selection and any shipped speech/AI layer must not depend on remote services. Cloud APIs may be used only as developer-side tooling outside the shipped runtime, never as a gameplay dependency.
decisions.rationale: The project owner explicitly stated that the game is offline and that the intelligent-NPC system must be offline at its foundation.

decisions.title: All Part I characters participate in the living-NPC layer
decisions.resolution: Treat living intelligence as a world-wide character rule, not a one-NPC demo. Named story characters receive rich biography, memory, relationships and knowledge envelopes; secondary named characters receive lighter persistent context; ambient populations use cheap archetype intelligence. All tiers remain offline and react to chapter mood, danger, weather and local context.
decisions.rationale: The project owner explicitly wants conversations with any character to feel like that character understands who they are, what has happened, and whether the surrounding world is peaceful, suspicious, grieving or at war.

decisions.title: PR #53 is the single CP56 mega-integration continuation path
decisions.resolution: Continue CP56/Work changes on PR #53 only. Keep develop unchanged until the current PR #53 head passes required validation.
decisions.rationale: One active integration branch prevents conflicting versions while we repair against one Actions result.

decisions.title: Adopt an exact-SHA automated quality gate without overstating proof
decisions.resolution: Extend the existing automation-first path instead of replacing it. Before merge, the exact candidate SHA should accumulate required evidence for Pre-Unreal/static checks, UE4.27 compile/import, startup/headless runtime, P1C01-P1C08 chapter audits, warning debt, story/route and save/load roundtrips, offline NPC behavior, text/localization integrity, plus target-device performance and memory evidence as those tests are implemented. Keep the established 720p Low-Medium 30 FPS floor target. Validate story consistency against project authorities (Governor, Story Canon Bible and FilmExperiencePlan). Produce machine-readable exact-SHA status plus a human-readable report. Introduce Unreal Automation Framework, Gauntlet and Unreal Insights incrementally where useful; do not discard proven Python/runtime checks or let test infrastructure replace game production.
decisions.rationale: The owner reviewed a programmer proposal for comprehensive automated quality checking and accepted the useful direction with project-specific corrections: exact evidence rather than absolute zero-bug claims, the existing 30 FPS target rather than an invented 60 FPS target, and project canon as the story authority.

decisions.title: Screenplays ground context, not verbatim runtime dialogue
decisions.resolution: Treat the supplied Fellowship and Two Towers screenplay PDFs as primary scene/dialogue-context references. Store derived chronology, mood, safe topics and future-knowledge blocks. Runtime dialogue stays original and bounded; the shipped game never needs the PDFs. Part I contexts are active now and Part II contexts are reference seeds until its runtime production begins.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants conversation to feel naturally embedded in the film world and broader than fixed scripted exchanges without requiring exact wording.

decisions.title: Use shader-compile time for non-blocking static/content expansion without bypassing the merge gate
decisions.resolution: While the target machine is busy compiling shaders or otherwise unavailable for UE rebuilds, continue work that can be statically reviewed: data contracts, dialogue coverage, exploration envelopes, source hygiene and validators. Keep the same PR #53 integration path and still require the final exact head to pass full UE4.27 validation before develop merge.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly asked not to sit idle while Unreal compiles shaders, but also wants broken gates repaired before integration.

decisions.title: Adopt Journey Discovery rewards instead of generic exploration XP
decisions.resolution: Use a first-time Journey Discovery system inspired by the satisfaction of discovery rewards in exploration RPGs, but fit it to this project's tone: brief discovery toast, Journey Insight, Chronicle/map/knowledge/companion unlocks and regional completion bonuses. Do not use raw combat-stat inflation, canon-changing rewards or story skips.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants the project to function as a complete exploration game as well as a playable film-spine experience.

decisions.title: Side content is off-camera film-context gap-fill, never an alternate story
decisions.resolution: Keep all mandatory story events and outcomes on the Peter Jackson film spine. Optional exploration may add original side games and moments only when they plausibly fit the same story window, location, available characters, knowledge state and emotional/danger context. Treat them as off-camera moments that could have happened between film scenes. They may reward exploration and deepen relationships/world knowledge, but cannot invent a competing major plot or alter canon.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants a complete game, not a film-only corridor, while explicitly rejecting deviation from the film's main story.

decisions.title: Raise the world visual bar above the earlier plain reference examples
decisions.resolution: Do not treat the previously shown external game screenshots as the final visual target. Aim for a more beautiful, cinematic and memorable Middle-earth presentation with strong vistas, layered terrain, richer materials/vegetation, water, atmosphere, lighting and chapter-specific visual identity. Achieve the higher beauty bar selectively and efficiently so the established 720p Low-Medium / 30 FPS target is not silently abandoned.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly rejected the earlier reference-image quality as not beautiful enough and wants a substantially more attractive world.

decisions.title: The Ring quest is the central state line; all other routes serve or surround it
decisions.resolution: Treat the One Ring as the persistent strategic/emotional axis. Frodo is the Part I bearer after Bilbo's transfer; parallel routes cannot become replacement Ring routes. The Part I split hands forward the Frodo/Sam Ring journey.
decisions.rationale: Owner explicitly reaffirmed the Ring as the axis of the series/game.

decisions.title: Use a dual-source character pipeline with provenance instead of waiting for one perfect external model
decisions.resolution: For each character, prefer a usable permitted external/project-owned base when available; otherwise build the character from legally usable/custom parts. External free/personal-use assets still require source and terms to be recorded before integration.
decisions.rationale: Owner wants immediate production and has multiple free/personal-use sources available, with custom 3D character creation as fallback.

decisions.title: Owner cinematic forest reference defines the higher environment beauty direction
decisions.resolution: Target the reference's dense naturalism, layered depth, strong light shafts, ground detail and embedded characters as the beauty direction, while using selective hero detail and optimization to preserve the 720p Low-Medium / 30 FPS floor.
decisions.rationale: Owner explicitly chose the supplied image as a better visual model than prior examples.

decisions.title: Treat the project as a modern narrative game wrapped around immutable film anchors
decisions.resolution: Mandatory Peter Jackson film anchors remain fixed. Between anchors, the game may add original plausible side missions, world events, exploration, companion activities, environmental puzzles, lightweight character-life systems and utility/content progression. These systems may deepen play but may not skip, reorder or alter film outcomes.
decisions.rationale: Owner explicitly asked to research what modern games contain and adopt fitting game systems throughout the project while keeping the film itself intact.

decisions.title: Film scenario is the non-negotiable story authority from beginning to end
decisions.resolution: For every mandatory story beat, scene order, character presence and outcome must follow the Peter Jackson film continuity. When screenplay/film source material is available, it must be checked before implementation; memory or invented connective logic may not override it. Original game content is permitted only in unused gaps around fixed anchors and must close or yield when the next canonical scene begins.
decisions.rationale: Owner explicitly reaffirmed that adherence to the film scenario from beginning to end is the highest story requirement and corrected any tendency to drift.

decisions.title: Do not make Frodo the default viewpoint when the film gives another character the action
decisions.resolution: Use Gandalf, Aragorn, Arwen, Boromir, Legolas, Gimli, Merry, Pippin, Sam and later-film characters as playable viewpoints when the film naturally centers the relevant action on them. Frodo remains the Ring-quest center, not the only playable character. Small original missions may expand verified gaps but may not displace fixed film scenes or outcomes.
decisions.rationale: Owner explicitly wants to exploit the trilogy's many non-Frodo mission opportunities and expand them slightly as game content.

decisions.title: Use four continuity classes plus explicit source-verification status
decisions.resolution: Classify side content as FILM_CORE, FILM_EXPANDED, FILM_INTERSTITIAL or BOOK_CHRONICLE. Track source verification separately. Book Chronicles never silently alter the main film timeline, and Part III stays FUTURE_SOURCE_CHECK until exact source verification is recorded.
decisions.rationale: The programmer proposal is valuable but a three-label system alone cannot distinguish original gap-fill from book-only alternate continuity or verified from unverified material.

decisions.title: Execute the project through one dependency-ordered master roadmap
decisions.resolution: All accepted unfinished work must be assigned to Data/MasterExecutionRoadmap.json. The roadmap is subordinate to ProjectGovernor and cannot override canon, evidence or requirement status. Large implementation continues in bundles: exact-head stability, Part I story/gameplay completeness, production characters/world, living-world/presentation polish, acceptance/performance, then source-verified Part II and Part III.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly asked to consolidate the large request set and begin large-scale work immediately without forgotten workstreams.

decisions.title: Adopt a layered Unreal automated QA immune system without replacing runtime/device/human proof
decisions.resolution: Use layered validation: static/pre-Unreal guards, UE Automation Framework tests, existing end-to-end runtime smoke/state/chapter audits, then target-device performance/soak and owner PIE/visual/pacing confirmation. Prefer deterministic authored probes and evidence-based thresholds over random tests or arbitrary global limits.
decisions.rationale: The external proposal is high-value, but several literal thresholds and test methods would create false confidence or false failures on this project's generated worlds and low-spec target.

decisions.title: Use measured hybrid visual-performance architecture instead of one-size-fits-all UE4 optimization recipes
decisions.resolution: Keep current async chapter banks and HISM/culling foundations. Prefer soft references, instancing, role-appropriate LODs, shared material-instance families and event/timer-driven logic. Use baked/static lighting, Distance Field Shadows, Cull Distance Volumes or World Composition only where the authored world topology and target-device measurements justify them.
decisions.rationale: The programmer proposal contains strong industry practices, but runtime-generated chapter geometry and the ~2 GB VRAM target make blanket lighting/world-streaming prescriptions unsafe.

decisions.title: Consolidate recent approved work into one comprehensive integration train
decisions.resolution: Use integration/comprehensive-foundation-v1 as the ordered convergence branch. Integrate startup grounding -> QA foundation -> performance guardrails -> V10 living-world content -> transactional transition coordination, validate exact head, then merge to develop. Do not independently merge overlapping #62/#63/#64/#65/#66 while the train is active.
decisions.rationale: Multiple individually useful branches now overlap the same runtime and governance surfaces. A single ordered integration train reduces regression risk and stops the project from spending more time on parallel repair branches than on coherent construction.

decisions.title: Adopt warehouse-first trilogy production in parallel with the P1C01 vertical slice
decisions.resolution: Maintain a comprehensive F1-F3 asset warehouse continuously instead of deferring final characters/world/audio to the end. Preproduction, sourcing and asset-bank construction may proceed across the trilogy in parallel, while runtime feature/chapter integration remains subject to the active foundation and exact-head gates. P1C01 Shire is the first fully assembled natural-looking benchmark used to prove the pipeline before mass application.
decisions.rationale: The project accumulated strong backend/governance coverage faster than visible production content. Warehouse-first production prevents recurring surprise gaps and turns asset acquisition/authoring into a persistent production lane rather than an ad hoc late task.

decisions.title: Separate warehouse intake validation from runtime acceptance
decisions.resolution: Run asset-warehouse filling continuously and independently from runner availability. Discovery, download/staging and catalogue enrichment do not wait for compile/PIE/device tests. Use a lightweight intake gate before READY_FOR_IMPORT; reserve UE4 import/build, PIE, performance and human visual/audio acceptance for assets that are actually integrated into a production slice.
decisions.rationale: Blocking warehouse fill on runtime gates wastes parallelizable production time; skipping all intake checks, however, converts the warehouse into an untrusted dump. The correct large-team pattern is staged asset ingestion with escalating proof requirements.

decisions.title: Parallelize world foundations beyond the Shire
decisions.resolution: Keep P1C01 as the first full production benchmark, but build reusable world foundations and warehouse stock in parallel for all major trilogy regions. This includes regional architecture, terrain/materials, vegetation/ecology, props, population/faction families, audio, lighting, VFX and traversal/collision contracts. Runtime Part II/III chapter implementation remains gated.

decisions.title: Third-person embodied perspective is the permanent gameplay default
decisions.resolution: Keep Shire Journey as a direct-control third-person action-adventure experience, broadly comparable in camera relationship to GTA V / Red Dead style play: behind or slightly over the active character with contextual camera tuning. Do not turn normal gameplay into top-down, isometric, RTS or squad-command control. Allow bounded cinematic camera shots only when they return cleanly to the player's embodied perspective.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants the game's central feeling to be inhabiting and touching Middle-earth, not observing it from above.

decisions.title: Reuse proven CI evidence without repeating expensive work
decisions.resolution: Use three validation cost classes: safe governance/docs/offline metadata inherits valid nearby green proof without UE execution; ordinary runtime/C++/Data/SourceAssets uses core build/import/Automation/runtime/warning validation without cook/package; Config/Build.cs/Target.cs/streaming/package/cook/release changes use the full package lane. If the immediate parent was cancelled, governance-only ancestry may search backward for the nearest green first-parent proof only when every intervening path is explicitly safe. Validation-policy-only classifier/Pre-Unreal edits may inherit a green parent without engine repetition.
decisions.rationale: Two days of W00 stabilization showed that repeating already-proven build/cook/package work wastes time and increases runner exposure without increasing confidence when only metadata changed. Evidence reuse must remain fail-closed and path-bounded so speed never weakens correctness.

decisions.title: Separate private-offline asset intake from distributable framework clearance
decisions.resolution: For the owner's private offline Shire Journey experience, uncertain or non-commercially-cleared art/audio may be classified and used only in an explicitly isolated PRIVATE_OFFLINE_ONLY lane without blocking local experimentation solely on commercial-license uncertainty. Such assets must remain tagged, replaceable and excluded from every distributable/commercial Framework package. The distributable Framework lane remains strict: only assets with clear redistribution/commercial entitlement may ship. Provider-access restrictions remain independent and binding: do not bypass authentication, paywalls, DRM, anti-bot controls or prohibited scraping.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants maximum private-production speed while preserving a clean framework that may later be sold. Classification/isolation is safer than deleting provenance or globally disabling license/access guards.

decisions.title: Global playable-film doctrine for the entire game world and full story
decisions.resolution: This doctrine is GLOBAL across the entire Shire Journey game, from the opening of the story through the final ending, across every chapter, region, character arc, settlement, dungeon, battlefield, travel segment and world-state transition. Shire/P1C01 is only the first implementation benchmark, not the scope of the rule. The player must feel physically present inside the film-continuity world rather than watching a chain of cutscenes or playing an unrelated open world. Canon-defining story beats and locked outcomes remain immutable. Between those beats, every chapter and region must expose interactive safe windows for embodied third-person exploration, optional conversations, world/household interaction, side activities, NPC life, fauna, environmental storytelling and local choice whenever chronology permits. Control may enter bounded cinematic/set-piece moments when required, then return cleanly to the player. Optional actions may change flavor, local relationships, discovery, pacing or minor world state, but must not invalidate the film's causal spine or locked chapter outcome. World/NPC/prop/audio state must transition coherently before and after each canon beat so the player feels the consequences in the playable world.
decisions.example_contract: F1-01/Bag End remains only the first benchmark example of the global rule. The same pattern must be applied chapter-by-chapter across the full game world: identify locked canon beats, surround them with playable safe windows, preserve chronology/outcomes, and return control into a world state that reflects what just happened.
acceptance_criteria: The doctrine applies to every chapter and every major playable region from the beginning of the story through the final ending; Shire/P1C01 is not an exception or the sole target.
Every major chapter identifies its locked canon beats and the playable safe windows around them.
Every major region identifies the world-life, exploration, interaction and environmental systems needed to make the player feel present inside that part of the story.
No required chapter is implemented as cutscene-only when an interactive safe window can preserve canon.
No free-roam/side activity can alter an immutable film outcome or create a contradictory chronology.
After a canon beat, NPC/world/prop/audio state reflects the new story state when the player regains control.
Dialogue added inside safe windows is original project-authored text and does not copy Tolkien or film dialogue verbatim.
Cinematic control transitions are bounded and return to the embodied third-person player cleanly.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly clarified that this is not a Shire/P1C01-specific design idea. It is a whole-game doctrine covering the complete world and full narrative: the player should inhabit and interact with the film continuity everywhere, while recognized story outcomes still unfold correctly.

decisions.title: Adopt the 225-source Master External Resource Bible as the global production sourcing map
decisions.resolution: The 68-page SHIRE_JOURNEY_MASTER_EXTERNAL_RESOURCE_BIBLE_V1_2026-09-25, containing 225 classified sources, is adopted as a global production-sourcing authority for the entire game. It does not override story/canon bibles. Its role is to diversify and prioritize sources for environment materials, vegetation, characters, rigging, animation, VFX, audio, music, UI/fonts, Arabic localization, terrain/GIS, scanning, AI-assisted creation and production tooling. Sourcing proceeds category-first using A then B then C priority, with provider-access restrictions preserved. The project converts the Bible into structured registry entries and category-specific acquisition waves rather than browsing randomly or copying all sources wholesale.
implementation_contract: Data/MasterExternalResourceBibleAdoptionV1.json is the machine-readable adoption/triage layer.
Data/GlobalWarehouseSourceRegistryV2.json is expanded from the Bible with high-value sources and corrected disabled/legacy routes.
Production waves cover world surfaces, vegetation/biomes, character/animation, VFX, audio, music, terrain/scanning and Arabic/UI across the whole game.
REFERENCE_ONLY/QUARANTINE/DISABLED sources do not auto-promote into distributable production.
DEC-037 still governs PRIVATE_OFFLINE_ONLY vs DISTRIBUTABLE_FRAMEWORK asset isolation.
DEC-038 still governs whole-game playable-film canon-safe design; resources serve the story rather than altering it.
performance_contract: 1K/2K default runtime textures; 4K only for measured hero assets.
Production textures use PNG/TGA, preferably channel-packed.
Heavy runtime assets use soft references + FStreamableManager async loading.
Crowds use pooling; repeated world detail uses ISM/HISM + LOD/culling.
High-poly scans/vegetation require decimation/retopo/LOD/material-slot and overdraw review before integration.

decisions.title: Immediate develop integration and dead-branch self-cleanup
decisions.resolution: develop is the canonical and continuously current integration branch. Every completed temporary branch must be exact-head validated, merged into develop immediately, then have its remote ref deleted automatically. Post-merge cleanup must delete the exact merged PR head when its live remote SHA still equals the merged head SHA, then prune other zero-ahead refs. A moved remote head is preserved as new work. The only temporary exceptions are active PR heads or branches with verified unique unsalvaged commits.
implementation_contract: Use one short-lived single-purpose branch/PR for a coherent engineering wave; batch related multi-file changes before publishing to avoid superseded runs.
After exact-head required validation succeeds, merge the completed branch into develop immediately; do not accumulate completed branches waiting for later consolidation.
Branch Cleanup runs automatically after every merged PR close event on GitHub-hosted Windows.
The exact merged PR head ref is deleted immediately when the live remote SHA still equals github.event.pull_request.head.sha; if the ref moved, preserve it as new work.
After exact-head closeout, Branch Cleanup enumerates live remote refs once and auto-deletes every non-protected, non-active-PR zero-ahead branch.
Branches with ahead_by > 0 are retained only for selective salvage/supersession and must not become alternate trunks.
GitHub is the live authority for PR/branch/workflow transport state; the Governor stores durable policy, execution order and evidence boundaries only.
decisions.evidence_boundary: Branch/process governance only; no gameplay acceptance claim.

decisions.title: Smart-fence acceleration for the massive production build
decisions.resolution: Parallel preparation lanes are authorized. Administrative friction is downgraded only where runtime correctness cannot be affected: missing not-yet-acquired candidates, non-final naming and private-offline commercial-clearance uncertainty may remain warnings or pending states. Technical safety stays strict. Runtime integration remains one PR at a time.
implementation_contract: Data/FastProductionSmartFenceV1.json defines blocking versus warning rules per lane.
Data/ProjectSourcePdfRegistryV1.json fingerprints the supplied source corpus and preserves authority roles.
Data/P1C01MaterialImportWaveV1.json selects a benchmark-first open-material wave.
Scripts/prepare_p1c01_material_intake.ps1 treats missing warehouse sources as pending but fails on technical payload defects.
Scripts/promote_p1c01_material_intake.ps1 uses a temporary SourceAssets/Production overlay and invokes the existing UE4 importer only on explicit request.
decisions.evidence_boundary: Preparation/tooling implementation only until a real local intake/import run emits its receipt/log. No COMPILE/PIE/DEVICE/VISUAL/PERFORMANCE acceptance is implied.

decisions.title: Route static and repository-administration CI off the supervised UE4 runner
decisions.resolution: Pre-Unreal and Branch Cleanup are event-driven on GitHub-hosted windows-latest using exact isolated checkouts. Unreal Build Validation and persistent Warehouse work remain on the supervised Windows runner where engine or persistent local state is required. This supersedes the earlier self-hosted static/admin routing while preserving the same fail-closed project validation and branch-safety contracts.
decisions.evidence_boundary: Current workflow/source configuration is guarded by PG-167/PG-176; runtime/PIE/device/visual/performance acceptance is unchanged.

decisions.title: Warehouse staging follows develop on the supervised runner
decisions.resolution: Remove the GitHub-hosted delta/no-stage jobs and obsolete push branch from warehouse-stage.yml. Relevant develop/PR warehouse changes directly queue one supervised Windows staging job with its own concurrency group.
decisions.evidence_boundary: Workflow/source configuration only until the supervised runner executes a staging job.

decisions.title: Launch P1C01 D with a bounded Mega Asset Promotion lane
decisions.resolution: Start P1C01 D as the sole runtime-changing lane from the merged C4 baseline: fixed authored lighting/sky/fog plus low-cost Shire water. In parallel, activate the existing P1C01 warehouse promotion queue for staging and intake QC only. No warehouse candidate may jump to READY_FOR_IMPORT, IMPORTED, INTEGRATED or ACCEPTED without its required provenance, format and technical evidence.
implementation_contract: D preserves fixed chapter-authored states; no free-running day/night cycle, per-frame sky/reflection recapture, planar-reflection default, per-frame CPU water simulation, quest/save topology change or LivingWorld ownership change.
The water presentation uses the existing project production material family and a resident-only soft chapter-bank path; runtime code does not synchronously load heavy production packages.
Mega Asset Promotion reuses Data/P1C01WarehousePromotionQueueV1.json and Data/ProductionAssetPromotionPolicyV1.json instead of creating a second inventory.
Animated final production assets remain FBX-only; OBJ is not accepted for animated final assets. Production textures are PNG/TGA; BMP cannot be promoted as final production texture evidence.
Promotion remains fail-closed: provider/source/license, staging receipt and SHA256 are required before READY_FOR_IMPORT, then class-specific QC before UE import/integration.
P1C01 remains the runtime benchmark; whole-game warehouse preparation may advance without authorizing Part II/III runtime expansion.
decisions.evidence_boundary: User direction authorizes implementation and staging/QC work only. No new PIE-TESTED, DEVICE-TESTED, VISUALLY-ACCEPTED, PACING-ACCEPTED or PERFORMANCE-ACCEPTED claim is created by this decision.
evidence: C4 candidate exact-head Unreal Build #875 SUCCESS

decisions.title: Eliminate redundant Unreal validation work without weakening exact-head quality gates
decisions.resolution: Administrative/non-runtime changes must not consume repeated full UE4.27 build/import/runtime/package cycles. Exact-head safety remains mandatory for runtime-relevant changes. Superseded runs from the same PR are cancelled, exact checkout preserves Git state for incremental UBT behavior, and a merged commit may inherit core proof only when its Git tree is exactly identical to a previously green parent tree.
implementation_contract: README/onboarding/handoff/classifier-test administrative paths stay on Pre-Unreal and do not trigger Unreal Build Validation by themselves.
Exact checkout preserves .git, fetches and hard-resets to TARGET_SHA, verifies HEAD exactly, and removes authenticated remote credentials after classification.
Git fetch uses a bounded low-speed cutoff and three attempts; stalled transfer cannot hold the device indefinitely.
Concurrency cancels only superseded runs from the same PR branch; unrelated runtime PR/develop runs are not cancelled.
Tree-equivalent proof reuse requires exact Git tree SHA equality plus a successful required Unreal proof on the identical parent tree.
Config/Build.cs/Target.cs/streaming/package/cook/release/unknown changes remain fail-safe FULL.
Runtime/source/data deltas continue through asset/core/full validation according to impact.
Do not increase compile parallelism or add blind binary caches until the safer structural reductions are measured.
decisions.rationale: Measured logs showed repeated 13-18 minute jobs for administrative changes, #888 spending ~11 minutes in checkout before cancellation, and repeated 238-252 second 76-action C++ rebuilds. The waste came from trigger/classifier/checkout architecture rather than insufficient quality checks.
decisions.evidence_boundary: CI source architecture only until a fresh corrected run measures actual checkout/build/total durations. No gameplay, PIE, device, visual, pacing or performance acceptance is implied.
evidence: Git tree equality: develop@2845071119d926defd6ba94c970f43729bc51674 == C4 green candidate bc1e04062d8079fef73eae64f68c81772b4fc56c tree 3de99fa7951e889cf319e967a2225e962d9cc554

decisions.title: Re-architect validation lanes around one persistent Unreal workspace
decisions.resolution: The dedicated UE4 runner keeps one persistent Unreal workspace for incremental C++/asset/runtime validation. GitHub-hosted Pre-Unreal and Branch Cleanup use isolated RUNNER_TEMP checkouts; Runner Health and self-hosted Warehouse source checkouts remain isolated from the persistent Unreal workspace. Administrative changes are removed from the Unreal trigger where safe, superseded same-PR work is cancelled, and exact-tree proof reuse avoids rebuilding byte-identical merge content.
implementation_contract: Pre-Unreal runs on GitHub-hosted windows-latest with an exact isolated RUNNER_TEMP checkout and never touches the supervised Unreal workspace.
Runner Health uses an isolated source checkout and never deletes the Unreal workspace.
Branch Cleanup runs on GitHub-hosted windows-latest with an isolated exact-head checkout and never consumes the UE4 runner.
Warehouse Stage remains self-hosted, uses an isolated source checkout, and keeps persistent downloaded payloads under D:\actions-runner\_warehouse\ShireJourney.
Only Unreal Build Validation owns the persistent project workspace used by UBT incremental detection.
Every coherent engineering wave should be committed atomically when tooling permits; avoid multiple sequential commits that create superseded CI runs.
Failure triage must classify GAME_RUNTIME, VALIDATOR_POLICY, CI_INFRA or ADMIN_GOVERNANCE before runtime code is changed.
No blind cache restore, compile parallelism increase or gate removal is authorized until structural waste reductions are measured.
decisions.rationale: Recent logs showed that lightweight workflows repeatedly deleted the same self-hosted GITHUB_WORKSPACE, destroying Git/UBT continuity and forcing 76-action editor rebuilds. Recent failure history also showed a large cancellation/governance/infra share rather than repeated gameplay regressions.
decisions.evidence_boundary: Architecture/source review only. Fresh exact-head measurements are required before claiming CI speed improvement. No PIE/device/visual/pacing/performance acceptance is implied.
evidence: Epic UBT adaptive Git working-set guidance and GitHub Actions concurrency guidance

decisions.title: Use GitHub Pro as a private-repository safety and tooling multiplier without re-architecting the proven Unreal lane
decisions.resolution: Adopt GitHub Pro benefits selectively where they materially improve Shire Journey: prioritize private branch protection/status-check enforcement and repository insights; keep full UE4.27 validation on the free self-hosted Windows runner; reserve the 3,000 hosted Actions minutes for lightweight isolated automation if hosted reliability is proven; use Codespaces only for non-engine repository work; use Packages only for small tooling; keep Pages/Wiki non-authoritative and unpublished for private project material unless the owner explicitly changes that policy.
implementation_contract: Do not move Unreal Build Validation to GitHub-hosted runners merely to consume the Pro minute allowance.

When branch protection is configured, develop/main must block force-push and deletion and should require the appropriate exact-head CI checks. Human review is not mandatory while there is only one maintainer.
Do not require CODEOWNER approval from the PR author; enable reviewer enforcement only after a second trusted maintainer exists.
Keep hosted Actions/Codespaces/Packages behind budgets and alerts; no silent paid overage.
Repository Insights may be used for CI/commit/contributor trend review without changing production authority.
GitHub Pages and Wiki must not duplicate ProjectGovernor/CURRENT_PROJECT_STATE or expose private/copyright-sensitive game material.
GitHub Pro is separate from GitHub Copilot Pro; no Copilot entitlement is assumed from this subscription.
Do not assume GitHub Code Security, private secret scanning, or private dependency review from personal Pro; those require separate eligible security licensing/plans.
Prefer a branch/tag ruleset or protected-branch policy for develop/main once repository-settings mutation is available; do not enable private push-ruleset assumptions that require Team.
decisions.rationale: The project is a private personal repository with heavy UE4.27 Windows validation and a supervised self-hosted runner. Pro's strongest immediate value is private-repository governance and additional optional hosted/tooling capacity, not replacing the engine/device lane. The policy therefore uses the new capabilities without reintroducing CI cost, merge deadlocks or a second source of truth.
decisions.evidence_boundary: OWNER UI-CONFIRMED GITHUB PRO + OFFICIAL GITHUB PLAN/RULESET DOCUMENTATION + CONNECTED-ACCOUNT/REPOSITORY FACTS. Subscription status is now directly confirmed by the owner's GitHub Billing UI. No payment identifiers are stored. No runtime/PIE/device/visual/performance claim is created.

decisions.title: Make the GitHub default-branch landing a zero-context redirect to the live develop Governor path
decisions.resolution: Keep main as stable/release and default-branch landing because repository scheduling/release behavior already depends on it, but make its README an explicit developer redirect to develop. On develop, README, PROJECT_GOVERNOR and the onboarding script must all identify Data/ProjectGovernor.json as the sole authority and must derive current work from live Governor fields rather than copied milestone prose.
implementation_contract: A person opening the repository on GitHub with no prior context must see, above the fold on main, that active development lives on develop.
The main landing README must point to the develop README/Governor/current-state path and tell a local clone to switch to develop before editing.
Develop README remains the canonical detailed entry page and the onboarding script remains a reader, never a second manager.
Docs/PROJECT_GOVERNOR.md must not hard-code a stale next production drop; current execution order comes from ProjectGovernor.execution_control and current_focus.
The onboarding script must warn when the checked-out branch is not the canonical development branch.
GitHub remains authority for volatile PR/branch/check state; ProjectGovernor remains authority for durable direction and proof boundaries.
decisions.evidence_boundary: ADMIN_GOVERNANCE / HANDOFF ONLY. This does not change runtime, content, PIE, device, visual, pacing or performance acceptance.

decisions.title: Lock the UE4 self-hosted runner to interactive-user watchdog ownership
decisions.resolution: The runner is not a Windows-service lane. Service-mode ownership is eliminated: actions.runner.* should be absent, or only Stopped+Disabled while pending deletion. UE4-27-Windows runs only under the proven interactive Windows user through ShireJourney-GitHubRunner-Watchdog. NETWORK SERVICE, LOCAL SERVICE and SYSTEM execution are forbidden.
implementation_contract: Never enable/start/reinstall actions.runner.* as an active Windows service.
install_runner_watchdog.ps1 must disable, stop and delete the legacy service registration before starting the watchdog.
runner_service_guard.ps1 must kill forbidden service-owned Runner.Listener/Runner.Worker processes and remove any recreated actions.runner.* service.
The watchdog Scheduled Task uses LogonType Interactive under the proven Windows user and continuously invokes the service guard.
verify_runner_session.ps1 must fail before heavy work unless the service is absent or Stopped+Disabled and the listener/worker belong to the interactive session.
A Work/AI session may inspect runner health but may not change runner ownership/topology without explicit owner authorization.
evidence: KNOWN/KF runner-broker history in ProjectGovernor and PROJECT_GUARDIAN
decisions.evidence_boundary: INFRASTRUCTURE OWNERSHIP POLICY + EXISTING STATIC GUARDS. This decision does not itself prove the current physical Windows service/task state; live runner health must be checked on the machine.

decisions.title: Remove the second runner execution path instead of repeatedly repairing it
decisions.resolution: Root-cause fix: the legacy Windows service registration is removed rather than kept Manual. The interactive watchdog owns the only supported runner path and continuously deletes any recreated service-mode path. This converts runner ownership from a procedural reminder into a self-enforcing machine invariant.
implementation_contract: One-time installer disables/stops/deletes actions.runner.* and installs the service guard beside the watchdog.
The watchdog runs the service guard at boot and on every supervision loop.
Service-owned Listener/Worker processes under NETWORK SERVICE/LOCAL SERVICE/SYSTEM are terminated.
Health validation accepts only service absent or stopped-disabled transitional state plus one interactive-user listener/worker topology.
Pre-Unreal PG-145B statically guards the service guard, installer, watchdog and verifier contracts.

Unreal #1000 exact-head job failed at Verify runner session health with RUNNER_HEALTH_FAIL service-identity identity=NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE.

decisions.evidence_boundary: ROOT-CAUSE RUNNER TOPOLOGY MACHINE-PROVEN on Unreal #1021 exact head. This is infrastructure proof only; the governance fast path skipped C++ build/import/PIE/package and creates no gameplay/device/visual/performance acceptance.

decisions.title: Freeze production trains until CI and warehouse repetition defects are removed
decisions.resolution: Stop active production PR churn and repair CI/warehouse architecture before resuming P1C01 production. Repeated warehouse PR runs and full archive extraction are treated as infrastructure defects, not as acceptable validation cost.
implementation_contract: No new production/runtime PR is opened while the repair branch is being hardened.
Warehouse Stage must not run on pull_request synchronize; it runs only after warehouse-impacting changes land on develop or by explicit manual dispatch.
Critical-gap intake QC inventories ZIP metadata without extracting every archive on every run.
Receipt reuse rejects structurally corrupt ZIPs; provider staging removes and redownloads corrupt cached archives before writing/reusing receipts.
Duplicate receipt rows are deduplicated before hashing/classification.
Blocked warehouse items print exact provider/asset/path/reason immediately.
Existing closed production branches remain preserved for later salvage; no completed runtime work is discarded.
evidence: Warehouse Stage #269/#270 repeated ~12-13 minute failures on PR #125.
Warehouse #270 blockers: duplicate AmbientCG Plaster007 corrupt ZIP central directory and KayKit extraction path failure.
decisions.evidence_boundary: INFRASTRUCTURE/CI ROOT-REPAIR SOURCE CHANGES ONLY. No new compile/PIE/device/visual/performance acceptance is created.

decisions.title: Split CI by proof type and preserve expensive build state unless invalidated
decisions.resolution: Use three distinct validation lanes: GitHub-hosted Pre-Unreal for static/policy proof, self-hosted Unreal only for engine/runtime deltas, and self-hosted Warehouse only after warehouse-impacting changes land on develop or explicit manual dispatch. Preserve Unreal intermediates by default and clean them only for build-rule/project-descriptor changes or bounded compile-recovery retry.
implementation_contract: Pre-Unreal runs on windows-latest and never consumes the supervised UE4 self-hosted runner.
Warehouse Stage has no pull_request trigger and classifies landed develop deltas so only affected providers/phases run.
Warehouse-only scripts/data are excluded from Unreal Build Validation triggers.
Unreal exact-head classification still fails safe to deeper proof when ancestry or delta classification is uncertain.
Reset project build intermediates only when SHIRE_RESET_INTERMEDIATES=true for Build.cs, Target.cs or project-descriptor invalidation; ordinary source/runtime changes keep UBT incremental state.
ci_build_unreal.cmd retains its one-time compiler-pressure recovery that clears intermediates only after a matching real compiler failure.

decisions.title: Adopt chapter-scale production packs and minimize workflow churn
decisions.resolution: Move P1C01 preparation from many tiny pushes/workflows toward chapter-scale packs: one large manifest and one warehouse workflow run may execute multiple bounded internal cars. Keep per-car quarantine, receipts and rollback boundaries while reducing PR/workflow frequency. Runtime/config/package-impacting changes retain exact-head Unreal gates; tooling-only changes use the cheapest proof lane that still covers their risk.
implementation_contract: P1C01MegaChapterPackV1 is the first chapter-scale pack and orchestrates inventory audit, mega promotion, material source export and character intake.
A chapter pack is large at the planning/staging layer but internally bounded; one blocked asset/car is quarantined and later independent cars continue.
Do not schedule legacy overlapping P1C01 audit/promotion/export/character steps in parallel with the chapter-pack step.
Prepare branches without opening PRs until a coherent batch is ready; prefer one PR/merge per coherent pack rather than repeated micro-PR churn.
Warehouse raw payloads remain local/persistent; Git receives selected production sources and receipts, not the entire raw warehouse.
Animated final production assets remain FBX-only; textures remain PNG/TGA; heavy runtime assets retain soft/async ownership; repeated detail retains ISM/HISM+LOD/culling.
No batch-size increase may bypass provenance, SHA256, format/QC, runtime, PIE, device, visual or performance evidence boundaries.
Binary/LFS policy changes are kept out of chapter-pack control-plane PRs when they would unnecessarily wake the Unreal lane; apply them in the first binary promotion wave that actually needs them.
decisions.rationale: The repository has accumulated thousands of workflow runs while the persistent warehouse already contains thousands of files and multi-gigabyte stock. Larger coherent packs reduce orchestration overhead without requiring unsafe monolithic runtime integration.

PR #138 Pre-Unreal #1303 SUCCESS and no Unreal Build trigger for tooling-only delta

decisions.title: Increase chapter-scale material source throughput with bounded item quarantine
decisions.resolution: Keep P1C01 material source promotion large and coherent without letting one oversized source abort the whole material car. The exporter uses a 32 MiB per-source ceiling and 256 MiB per generated-branch batch ceiling, quarantines individual over-budget sources, and may complete when at least six receipt-verified materials remain. Runtime texture sampling, UE import and target-device acceptance remain separate exact-head evidence lanes.
implementation_contract: MATERIAL_SOURCE_EXPORT receives its byte budgets from Data/P1C01MegaChapterPackV1.json.
Default chapter-pack budget is 32 MiB per source and 256 MiB per generated branch batch with minimum six exported materials.

An individual source that exceeds the single-file or remaining batch budget is recorded in P1C01MaterialSourceReceipt.json quarantine and does not abort the car unless the minimum exported count is no longer met.
PNG stays Git LFS tracked. TGA source export is quarantined until the repository has an explicit *.tga LFS rule in the binary promotion wave that first requires it.
Low-spec runtime material rule remains one base-color sample plus scalar Roughness/Metallic/Specular; this source-promotion budget does not authorize extra runtime texture samples.
No source-promotion success implies UE import, runtime binding, PIE, device, visual or performance acceptance.
decisions.rationale: Warehouse #278 proved the chapter pack itself can continue past a blocked car, but MATERIAL_SOURCE_EXPORT stopped on one SH_DIRT_SOIL base-color file exceeding the old 16 MiB limit after eight materials had already passed intake QC. A larger bounded source budget plus item-level quarantine preserves coherent high-throughput promotion while retaining explicit failure accounting.

Warehouse Stage #278: P1C01_MATERIAL_INTAKE_PASS prepared=8 pending=8 manual=0

decisions.title: Require explicit albedo semantics and selected-file provenance before P1C01 material import
decisions.resolution: Hold the generated P1C01 material source branch from UE import until material intake deterministically rejects support maps and ambiguous texture names from the visible base-color slot, and records provenance from the exact selected file rather than the first matching warehouse receipt row.
implementation_contract: Accepted visible color candidates must be PNG/TGA with explicit basecolor, albedo, diffuse/diff or color naming semantics.
Normal, AO/occlusion, roughness, metallic, height/displacement, ARM/ORM, preview and ambiguous texture names cannot become AlbedoTexture through fallback ranking.
Provenance is mapped per concrete candidate file; the generated receipt records selected_source_filename and selected_source_kind for the exact chosen visible-color source.
Items without an explicit albedo candidate remain pending or manual-queued; they do not block independent prepared materials.
The existing 32 MiB/source, 256 MiB/batch and minimum-six DEC-055 bounds remain unchanged.
Do not open the generated material branch for UE import until a post-merge Warehouse run regenerates the receipt under this rule.
decisions.rationale: Warehouse #279 successfully generated eight materials, but source review found that the intake code captured provenance from the first matching receipt row before final texture selection. The generated receipt therefore cannot prove that its source_url belongs to the exact selected base-color file; two wood entries show AO URLs. This is an evidence-quality blocker even if the selected bytes may be correct.
evidence: Scripts/prepare_p1c01_material_intake.ps1 pre-fix provenance assignment precedes Select-BaseColor
P1C01MaterialSourceReceipt.json wood_floor and wooden_floor_02 entries expose AO source URLs
decisions.evidence_boundary: SOURCE/QC DECISION. It does not assert that the already-generated PNG bytes are AO; it asserts that existing provenance cannot prove the exact selected source. Post-merge Warehouse regeneration is required before UE import.

decisions.title: Generated source branches publish with explicit remote-SHA leases
decisions.resolution: Generated warehouse source branches must not rely on an implicit force-with-lease remote-tracking ref. Before publishing, the producer reads the authoritative remote branch SHA with ls-remote and pushes with an explicit ref:SHA lease. New branches use a normal create push.
implementation_contract: Never use bare `git push --force-with-lease origin` for generated warehouse branches.
Resolve refs/heads/<generated-branch> directly from origin before publish.
If the remote branch exists, use `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<exact-remote-sha>`.
If the remote branch does not exist, create it without force.
Disable credential-helper persistence for ls-remote/push because workflow authentication is ephemeral and must not write to WinCred.
A real concurrent remote update after the lease lookup remains a hard publish failure; do not overwrite an unknown newer result.
Static validation must reject regression to implicit lease behavior.
decisions.rationale: Warehouse #281 completed intake and created a valid local material-source commit, then Git rejected publish as `stale info` because bare --force-with-lease used stale/missing local remote-tracking state. The failure was control-plane state, not source QC. Explicit remote-SHA leasing removes that hidden dependency while preserving race protection.
evidence: Warehouse #281 local generated commit 2474500 created 17 files before publish
Warehouse #281 Git error: HEAD -> generated/p1c01-material-source-v1 (stale info)
decisions.evidence_boundary: CONTROL-PLANE ROOT-CAUSE FIX. Exact-head Pre-Unreal and post-merge Warehouse rerun are required before publish is run-proven.

decisions.title: Run P1C01 closure as one maximum-throughput chapter source pack
decisions.resolution: Move P1C01 source acquisition/preparation to one large closure pack that stages all currently authorized public/open provider stock needed for Shire world, materials, props, nature, audio, fauna and character/animation support, then prepares/promotes it through bounded internal cars. Maximize raw Warehouse throughput, but keep Git/LFS source promotion and UE import bounded separately.
implementation_contract: One P1C01 Chapter Closure Mega Pack V2 may stage Poly Haven, ambientCG, Quaternius, Kenney, KayKit and authorized OpenGameArt stock in one Warehouse workflow.
Provider/asset/source blockers quarantine only their car; infrastructure/storage/inventory corruption remains hard-fail.
Persistent Warehouse may grow by multiple GB; minimum free-disk reserve is enforced and original staged payloads are never deleted to make room.
Large material source promotion is capped at 640 MiB with 48 MiB per source and at least 18 receipt-verified materials; raw Warehouse size is not copied wholesale into Git.
Runtime import remains a later bounded lane; no chapter pack may force UE to synchronously load the raw Warehouse.
Animated final candidates remain FBX; production textures PNG/TGA; heavy runtime assets soft+async; crowds/fauna pooled; repeated world detail ISM/HISM+LOD+culling.
Legacy overlapping P1C01 staging/promotion/export/intake workflow steps are suppressed while Closure Pack V2 runs.
Part II/III runtime remains closed; only reusable source stock may be prepared outside P1C01.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly authorized maximum practical batch size to accelerate Shire construction. Current Warehouse already holds multi-GB stock and the V1 chapter pack proved car-level quarantine. The safe acceleration path is larger source acquisition/preparation, not one unbounded UE import or a monolithic hard-reference content dump.

Warehouse #279: V1 chapter pack passed 4 / 0 / 0 and generated 8 material sources.
Warehouse #281: material intake passed prepared=8 pending=8 manual=0 before publish-control failure.
decisions.evidence_boundary: SOURCE/CONTROL-PLANE DECISION. Exact-head static validation and a post-merge Warehouse V2 run are required before the large closure pack is RUN-PROVEN. UE import/PIE/device/visual/performance remain separate.

decisions.title: Parse every repository PowerShell script before merge
decisions.resolution: Add a hosted Pre-Unreal parser gate that parses every Scripts/**/*.ps1 file with the Windows PowerShell parser before project validation. Parser errors are merge blockers and must be fixed at source.
implementation_contract: Pre-Unreal runs Scripts/test_powershell_syntax.ps1 on every exact head.
The parser gate recursively covers repository PowerShell scripts under Scripts.
Any parser error reports file, line, column, message and offending text, then exits non-zero.
PowerShell parser-gate changes remain tooling-only and do not wake Unreal Build.
A syntax failure is never classified as an asset/provider blocker; it is control-plane/source failure and must be repaired before merge.
decisions.rationale: Warehouse #282 failed before material execution because the generated-branch exporter contained an unterminated PowerShell string/if block. Pre-Unreal #1317 had passed because repository validation checked semantic markers but never invoked the PowerShell parser on all scripts. The durable fix is a parser gate, not another one-off string repair.
decisions.evidence_boundary: SOURCE/CI PREVENTION. The new parser gate requires exact-head Pre-Unreal proof. It does not imply Warehouse, UE, PIE, device or visual acceptance.

implementation_contract: Restore Scripts/runner_watchdog.ps1 byte-for-byte from commit 1066cf022723fcdef9bfac66519f5b0f9c1e03a4.
Keep the repository-wide parser gate active so any future PowerShell corruption blocks merge.

decisions.title: Isolate long P1C01 closure execution from the normal Warehouse train
decisions.resolution: Keep the normal Warehouse workflow on its proven short/cancellable contract and move the 180-minute non-cancelling P1C01 closure train into a dedicated workflow with its own concurrency group and fast preflight.

The long closure workflow and normal selective Warehouse workflow have separate concurrency groups.

decisions.title: Preflight and bounded-retry UE production asset saves
decisions.resolution: Before UE production import, perform a cheap destination-health check that rejects active editor processes, verifies Content/Production write/delete ability, clears read-only only on untracked generated uassets, and exclusive-opens existing uassets. If the importer still exits on a file delete/save error, run the same preflight once and retry the importer exactly once.
implementation_contract: Never delete tracked production assets as part of recovery.
Never clear read-only on tracked Content/Production assets; fail with explicit evidence instead.
Retry only for importer file-save/delete failures and at most once.
Non-save/delete importer failures fail immediately.
A successful import still requires the commandlet's explicit 0 failures marker.
decisions.rationale: Unreal Build #1047 compiled ShireJourneyEditor successfully and imported 376 source files with the commandlet reporting 0 import failures, but the workflow still failed because UE could not delete/save Content/Production/Textures/T_Cloth_Green.uasset. The log does not prove whether the cause was read-only state or an exclusive file lock, so the durable fix is to measure both conditions before import and retry only the proven save/delete failure class.
decisions.evidence_boundary: SOURCE-IMPLEMENTED. Exact-head Unreal rerun is required before COMPILE/IMPORT success can be claimed.

decisions.title: Rebuild watchdog service guard on clean source and keep closure preflight off Unreal
decisions.resolution: Use the clean watchdog body as the base, then reapply only the required continuous service-ownership guard hooks. Keep closure-only preflight scripts in Unreal paths-ignore and fix the PG-193 workflow-path assertion to match the actual workflow text.
implementation_contract: runner_watchdog.ps1 contains ServiceGuardPath, Invoke-ServiceOwnershipGuard, Invoke-RunnerServiceGuard and SHIRE_RUNNER_WATCHDOG_SERVICE_GUARD_TRIGGER on a single non-duplicated script body.
The service guard runs once at watchdog boot and once per watchdog loop before listener recovery logic.
p1c01 closure preflight tooling remains excluded from Unreal Build push and pull_request filters.
PG-193 checks for the actual test_powershell_syntax.ps1 workflow reference rather than a doubly escaped literal.
Exact-head Pre-Unreal must pass before this repair is considered STATIC-VALIDATED.
decisions.rationale: Pre-Unreal #1332 showed seven static failures after the earlier watchdog restoration. Five were expected because the clean historical watchdog lacked later service-guard hooks; one was a missing Unreal paths-ignore entry for the new closure preflight; one was a validator string-escaping bug. The correct repair is to reconstruct the required service guard on top of the clean source instead of restoring the previously corrupted later file.

Pre-Unreal #1332: PG-192 missing closure preflight Unreal paths-ignore

decisions.title: Sequential two-chapter production queue keeps P1C01 active and P1C02 gated behind Gate 6/7
decisions.resolution: Keep P1C01 Shire/Hobbiton/Bag End as the sole active runtime closure chapter. Once that gate is accepted, the sequential queue may automatically begin P1C02 source preparation without another owner continue prompt.

P1C02 source/warehouse preparation may exist early; P1C02 runtime integration may not.
Reuse valid Shire/Bag End stock before acquiring duplicate P1C02 assets.
Every queued heavy wave starts with a cheap preflight.
SEQUENTIAL_CHAPTER_QUEUE_WAIT is an expected green waiting state while P1C01 Gate 6/7 is not ACCEPTED.

decisions.title: Extend existing living-world architecture with bounded systemic environmental reactions
decisions.resolution: Adopt AAA Visual Quality + Systemic Reactivity + Intelligent NPCs + Living World + Strict Optimization as the durable production direction. Preserve the existing LivingWorldDirector/NPCContext/Quest/WorldRouter ownership split and add future environmental reaction capability as a small bounded event/responder contract rather than a second world-intelligence brain.

LivingWorldDirector owns coarse population/event budgets, pooling, activation and chapter-aware world activity; it does not own every object's local reaction.
ShireNPCContextSubsystem owns bounded NPC context projection; ShireQuestSubsystem remains quest/story/memory truth.
World/story systems may publish bounded events such as Hit, Interact, PlayerNear, WeatherChanged, DangerChanged and StoryStateChanged; supported responders own local visual/audio reaction.
No full-rate Tick or full physics simulation for every tree, plant, prop or ambient actor.
Prefer WPO/material response, pooled transient FX/audio, delegates/timers and distance/activity budgets.
Runtime implementation is deferred until the active P1C01 closure train reaches the appropriate integration step and remains subject to Gate 6/7 and target-device performance evidence.
