decisions.title: Unreal validation waits on editor and commandlet ownership before production import
decisions.resolution: Replace the editor-only wait assumption with a shared UE4 process wait/diagnostic contract that observes both UE4Editor and UE4Editor-Cmd. Never kill an interactive editor by name. Recover only a bounded stale CI-owned commandlet when workspace ownership, unattended commandlet signature, age and orphan-parent evidence all agree.
implementation_contract: Observe both UE4Editor and UE4Editor-Cmd before build/import-sensitive steps.
Emit PID, parent PID, session, owner, age and command line for blocking Unreal processes.
Never terminate UE4Editor by process name or merely because validation wants the machine.
A UE4Editor-Cmd may be force-stopped only when it is an old workspace-owned unattended ShireJourney CI commandlet with a recognized CI signature and no live parent.
Production-import preflight remains fail-closed if any Unreal process survives the wait/recovery contract.
Add a static regression guard so an editor-only wait cannot silently return.
decisions.rationale: Unreal Build #1068 compiled successfully, the wait step reported the editor closed, then production-import preflight immediately found PID 14144. Source inspection showed the wait step checked only UE4Editor while preflight checked UE4Editor and UE4Editor-Cmd. The mismatch explains the false-clear path without assuming PID ownership.
decisions.evidence_boundary: SOURCE-IMPLEMENTED. Fresh exact-head Pre-Unreal and Unreal validation are required before claiming the repair validated.

decisions.title: Prepare all Part I runtime chapters now while preserving canonical mission IDs and serialized runtime gates
decisions.resolution: Prepare shared-stock source indexes for downstream P1C02-P1C08 immediately, but preserve one runtime-changing chapter lane at a time. Treat F1-01..F1-08 from the supplied mission matrix as canonical story package IDs and P1C01..P1C08 as legacy runtime implementation boundaries until an explicit save/quest-safe migration is accepted.
implementation_contract: P1C01 remains the active runtime benchmark until real Gate 6/7 acceptance.
P1C02-P1C08 source/warehouse candidate indexing may run now from shared stock without duplicate per-chapter copies.
Only the immediate runtime successor opens after its predecessor Gate 6/7 status is ACCEPTED.
Do not rename or renumber existing runtime chapter IDs in place until save, quest, checkpoint and story-state migration is explicitly implemented and validated.
Preparation never becomes a READY_FOR_IMPORT or acceptance claim by metadata alone.

The supplied mission matrix and current FilmExperiencePlan reveal a non-one-to-one ID split, so a recorded reconciliation is required before automation can safely scale.
decisions.evidence_boundary: SOURCE/PREPARATION ARCHITECTURE. No downstream runtime, PIE, device, visual or performance acceptance is claimed.

decisions.title: Standing owner authorization for safe routine production execution
decisions.resolution: Routine reversible project work may continue without repeated owner 'continue/allow' prompts: inspection, safe fixes, branches, commits, PR updates, documentation, CI reruns, source/warehouse preparation and gate-compliant merges. Stop for owner input only at genuine human/external authority boundaries.

Still require owner action for login/OAuth, purchase/entitlement, unresolved licensing/canon conflicts, destructive no-rollback actions, or human Gate 6/7 evidence that cannot be manufactured by CI.
Platform-generated permission dialogs cannot be suppressed by repository policy; minimize operations that trigger them but never bypass platform authorization.
All runtime chapter advancement remains subject to existing quality gates regardless of standing execution authorization.

decisions.title: Production trains must use deterministic PowerShell 5.1 and native-command exit contracts
decisions.resolution: Closure/source-preparation trains may not depend on ambient LASTEXITCODE after non-native PowerShell work, may not truncate native git output inside a pipeline before exit capture, and must materialize generic-list output explicitly before JSON serialization on Windows PowerShell 5.1.
implementation_contract: P1C01 closure cars treat pure PowerShell scriptblocks as success unless they throw; native child PowerShell processes are wrapped by a helper that captures their explicit exit code and throws a typed failure.
Generated material branch remote-head lookup captures the complete git ls-remote output first, records the native exit code, retries at most three times, then parses the stored output.
Part I shared-stock candidate lists call ToArray() and bind to object[] before ordered-hashtable/JSON serialization.
Pre-Unreal PG-196 statically guards these three contracts.
Provider/source blockers may still quarantine and continue; infrastructure failures remain hard-stop.
No change in this decision weakens Gate 6/7, runtime serialization, canon authority or target-device acceptance requirements.
decisions.rationale: Develop runs after PR #145 exposed three deterministic production-train defects: closure storage preflight passed but StrictMode read an unset LASTEXITCODE; Warehouse #283 prepared and committed eight materials but remote-head lookup failed through a native-command pipeline; Part I prep failed in PowerShell 5.1 while embedding a generic List[object] into an ordered report. These are infrastructure/tooling defects, not content failures.

decisions.title: F1-04 Bree & Weathertop uses one shared mega source superpack for P1C02 and P1C03

decisions.title: Warehouse inventory corruption must emit exact mismatch evidence before repair
decisions.resolution: When warehouse inventory audit detects hash/license/missing-reference corruption, emit bounded exact evidence in the job log before failing. Do not auto-delete or rewrite payloads from a count-only failure.
implementation_contract: Hash mismatch log includes provider, batch, asset, record kind, path, declared hash and actual hash.
License hash mismatch log includes provider, batch, asset, path, declared hash and actual hash.

Only the first 20 rows per defect class are emitted to keep logs bounded.
Audit still exits nonzero and remains a hard stop until the corruption is explicitly repaired or quarantined with evidence.

decisions.title: Long CI waits must use bounded polling and asynchronous continuation
decisions.resolution: Interactive project work may not spin in repeated GitHub polling loops while a long-running CI job is in progress. Use bounded live checks, then hand continuation to CI/automation and continue independent safe work.
implementation_contract: Within one interactive response, perform at most two follow-up status polls for the same long-running workflow after the initial state read.

Use the scheduled Shire Journey continuation automation for later re-entry and root-cause handling.
When safe independent work exists, continue that work on a separate branch without modifying the exact head under validation.
A completed success/failure event may be handled immediately; only genuinely human-required blockers should interrupt the owner.
This rule changes orchestration only; it does not weaken exact-head validation, Gate 6/7, canon, or evidence requirements.
decisions.rationale: Repeated interactive polling of long Unreal and warehouse runs caused the conversation to appear stuck for extended periods even when CI itself was progressing normally. The project needs responsive orchestration without weakening verification.
evidence: PR #153 exact-head Pre-Unreal #1379 and Unreal #1095 both completed SUCCESS while repeated polling made the chat appear stalled.

decisions.evidence_boundary: ORCHESTRATION GOVERNANCE. Does not imply runtime, device, visual, or performance acceptance.

decisions.title: Warehouse provenance uses the latest valid receipt per normalized payload path
decisions.resolution: Preserve historical warehouse receipts, but resolve one active provenance record per normalized payload path. The newest parseable receipt record for that path is active; older records remain historical/superseded and do not compare stale hashes against a legitimately refreshed payload.
implementation_contract: Normalize payload paths before provenance grouping so Windows case and slash variations cannot create parallel active records for the same file.
Order records by staged_at_utc when parseable, fall back to receipt file LastWriteTimeUtc, and use deterministic receipt path/record-index tie breakers.
Only the active record participates in payload existence, payload SHA256, license snapshot SHA256, provider summary and duplicate-hash audit checks.
Superseded receipts remain on disk and are recorded in warehouse_inventory_latest.json with old/new batch and receipt identity; they are history, not audit failures.
If the active newest receipt disagrees with the current payload, the inventory audit still hard-fails with exact active receipt evidence.
Do not rewrite an old receipt and do not delete a payload merely to make the audit pass.
Pre-Unreal executes a synthetic PowerShell regression proving V1 stale-hash supersession, normalized-path coalescing and fail-closed behavior for a corrupted active V2 payload.
decisions.rationale: Warehouse #285 identified ambientCG\PLASTER\Plaster007_2K-PNG.zip with a historical WAREHOUSE_AMBIENTCG_P1C01_V1 hash beginning 3aa7dd while the current payload hash begins 7c486a. The modern ambientCG stager structurally validates the ZIP, hashes the current file and writes a newer V2 receipt. Auditing every historical receipt as simultaneously active incorrectly turns legitimate refresh history into corruption.
evidence: Warehouse #285 exact mismatch evidence for ambientCG\PLASTER\Plaster007_2K-PNG.zip
decisions.evidence_boundary: SOURCE-IMPLEMENTED repair contract. Fresh exact-head Pre-Unreal plus persistent warehouse inventory rerun are required before claiming the mismatch repaired or inventory clean.

decisions.title: Balanced-Medium visual quality and Deep Audit V1 become permanent engineering constraints
decisions.owner_direction: The game must remain visually attractive and enjoyable on the target laptop. 'Low-Medium' is not permission to make the image look cheap; use a balanced Medium baseline with selective High treatment for visually important content and save performance on lower-salience costs.
decisions.deep_audit_disposition: SHIRE JOURNEY PRE-MORTEM PERFORMANCE & ARCHITECTURE DEEP AUDIT V1 is adopted as a validation checklist, not as proof of ten defects. It reported zero confirmed code defects and ten plausible runtime risk surfaces requiring source/runtime measurement before acceptance.
engineering_rules: Preserve the 30 FPS floor, DX11, 720p, 8 GB RAM and ~2 GB VRAM target.
Prioritize perceived image quality for hero characters, nearby architecture, terrain readability, primary lighting and key materials.
Reduce cost first through measured distant-shadow ranges, far LOD/detail density, nonessential post/effects, culling and streaming/residency budgets rather than globally lowering all quality.
Treat settlement-entry streaming + NPC activation + AI/animation/collision + first-use rendering + GC as one compound performance envelope.
Use the Deep Audit R-01 through R-10 list as a falsifiable test matrix; do not relabel an UNSUPPORTED risk as a defect without source or runtime evidence.
Track p95/p99/max frame time and memory/residency behavior for target-device acceptance; average FPS alone is insufficient.

Existing async streaming, soft-reference ownership, pooled population, bounded save payload and target-device plans remain the preferred architecture and must be measured rather than rewritten speculatively.
decisions.evidence_boundary: GOVERNANCE/DESIGN DECISION only. It does not claim PIE, device, visual, pacing or performance acceptance.

update_protocol: Treat Data/ProjectGovernor.json as the first-read/last-write coordination record for any meaningful project change.
Read this file first before any meaningful gameplay, architecture, story or quality decision.

Promote only user requests/decisions that are explicitly accepted, confirmed or clearly agreed. Suggestions still under discussion, rejected ideas and options that do not fit the project remain non-authoritative unless later adopted.
For a contradiction: preserve both requirements and add/update one decision/open conflict here.
For implementation: update evidence/missing_work/status here only after repository evidence exists.
For testing: update region_quality and active_gate only from actual static/compile/PIE/device/human evidence.

external_review_findings.source: Programmer visual-quality/performance proposal supplied by owner
external_review_findings.claim: Use UE4.27 world/memory streaming, soft references, optimized lighting/materials, LOD/culling/HISM and event-driven logic to raise realism while preserving smooth performance on mid/low hardware.

already_present: UShireChapterAssetStreamingSubsystem uses FSoftObjectPath + FStreamableManager::RequestAsyncLoad for chapter/route asset banks.
AWorldDetailCluster uses UHierarchicalInstancedStaticMeshComponent with explicit cull distances and no actor Tick.
Shire foliage already uses hierarchical instancing; Fellowship V10 detail paths also use HISM clusters.
DeepProjectAudit already rejects a possible synchronous LoadObject inside Tick.
Major world builders are non-ticking construction actors.
accepted: Heavy production assets remain soft/asynchronous and residual synchronous LoadObject debt is burned down incrementally.
Repeated foliage/decorative detail uses HISM/ISM plus explicit distance culling instead of actor-per-detail density.
Shared master materials/material instances are preferred; dynamic instances are used only where runtime parameter variation is actually needed.
LOD and culling become production asset budgets, with engine-level validation added when final meshes are present.
Complex recurring logic should prefer events/delegates/timers or throttled updates over unnecessary every-frame Tick.
corrected: Do not replace the current ChapterWorldRouter + async chapter-bank architecture with World Composition merely because it is a common UE4 technique. Evaluate Level Streaming/World Composition only if later authored contiguous sublevels materially need it.

Baked Lightmass is not a blanket solution for the current runtime-generated chapter geometry. Use baked/static or stationary lighting selectively in future authored static sublevels/interiors; runtime-generated spaces retain measured dynamic lighting.
Distance Field Shadows are not assumed cheaper on the ~2 GB VRAM target. They require target-device comparison against bounded Cascaded Shadow Maps/static lighting before adoption.
Do not require automatic LOD on every tiny mesh regardless of screen size/instance strategy; require appropriate LOD/cull budgets by asset role.
Material Instances are preferred, not an absolute rule that every material must be a dynamic instance.

external_review_findings.next_action: Protect existing async/HISM/cull/tick discipline now; after startup/QA gates are healthy, profile target-device lighting, LOD, material, draw-call, streaming and transition budgets before selecting baked/distance-field/world-composition changes.

known_failures.symptom: UE4 BuildCookRun reaches NonUFS staging then fails copying Engine/Binaries/ThirdParty/DbgHelp/dbghelp.dll to the packaged staging destination with Access denied on the self-hosted Windows runner.
evidence: Unreal #627: cook/pak succeeded, dbghelp copy failed after staging retries.

Unreal #643 on d94b7fe7797e9ef417b7dad2abde26dfc279e700: stage-root preflight passed, UnrealPak exited 0, then SafeCopyFile repeatedly denied the destination Saved/W00Stage-36038731060-1/WindowsNoEditor/Engine/Binaries/ThirdParty/DbgHelp/dbghelp.dll under the NetworkService runner context.
Unreal #643: -nodebuginfo did not suppress bundled DbgHelp staging; UAT ended ExitCode=1 / BUILD FAILED.
Unreal #651 Attempt 2 on exact head efdb2e291505472247fae921945b083b3cc1ce2c completed the full automated chain successfully.
known_failures.rejected_workaround: Do not silently copy/replace dbghelp.dll, change the Data contract, or treat -nodebuginfo as sufficient.
known_failures.permanent_policy: When SHIRE_CI_NO_DEBUGINFO=1, ShireJourney.Target.cs sets WindowsPlatform.bUseBundledDbgHelp=false. ci_package_w00.ps1 separately proves source readability and exact destination writability before UAT, then waits for and propagates a concrete UAT exit code.
known_failures.reopen_rule: Reopen if a fresh exact-head package still requests bundled dbghelp.dll, the exact destination preflight fails, or UAT fails for another demonstrated staging cause.
known_failures.root_cause: The CI package policy relied on -nodebuginfo, but UE4.27 Windows Game packaging still stages its bundled DbgHelp copy unless the Game TargetRules disable it. The runner can write the stage root, yet the exact bundled-DLL destination copy is denied. The wrapper also failed to propagate that UAT failure because its observed process ExitCode was blank.

runner_execution_contract.required_identity_rule: Runner.Listener and Runner.Worker must belong to the same proven interactive Windows user/session as the job, with a live Explorer desktop session.
prohibited_actions_without_owner_authori: Do not run config.cmd with --runasservice or reinstall the runner as a Windows service.
Do not Start-Service, enable, or recreate actions.runner.*.
Do not switch the runner account to NETWORK SERVICE, LOCAL SERVICE, SYSTEM, or any non-interactive service identity.
Do not replace the watchdog Scheduled Task with service-mode execution.
Do not kill/restart Runner.Listener while Runner.Worker is active except through the repository watchdog's bounded recovery contract.
approved_recovery_path: Run install_runner_watchdog.ps1 once from an elevated interactive-user PowerShell; it disables/stops and deletes actions.runner.* service registration, kills forbidden service-owned runner processes, installs the permanent guard, and starts the interactive watchdog.
Use the interactive-user ShireJourney-GitHubRunner-Watchdog Scheduled Task as the only runner supervisor.
The watchdog invokes runner_service_guard.ps1 continuously so any recreated service-mode runner is stopped/deleted before it can own the UE4 lane.
Run repository runner-health verification before heavy Unreal/Warehouse work.
If topology is wrong, fail closed and report exact identity/service/task state; never improvise service mode.
runner_execution_contract.rationale: The recurring failure was architectural, not a one-off: keeping a registered Manual Windows service left a second runnable ownership path that another Work/admin action could start. NETWORK SERVICE then owned Runner.Listener and broke UE4 validation. The permanent design removes that second execution path and continuously polices its return.

permanent_self_heal.watchdog_behavior: Detect any actions.runner.* service or service-owned Runner.Listener/Runner.Worker and purge it before continuing.

story_source_execution_contract.owner_intent: Let the player live the LOTR journey in depth rather than consume a shortened chain of major scenes.
story_source_execution_contract.timeline_role: Navigation/order spine for the whole trilogy; never a maximum-detail specification.
story_source_execution_contract.film_screenplay_role: Primary authority for film-driven chronology, visible staging, participating characters, knowledge ceilings and locked outcomes.
story_source_execution_contract.tolkien_role: Primary supplied source for deeper compatible lore, geography, cultures, chronology, relationships, material culture, journey detail and book-only events.
story_source_execution_contract.book_only_gameplay_rule: If Tolkien contains an event/detail omitted or compressed by the films and it can fit without changing a required film outcome, chronology, character knowledge or route integrity, treat it as a playable-content candidate rather than discarding it by default.
source_packet_required_layers: Timeline chapter ID, critical beat, safe window and locked outcome
Matching film/screenplay scene order, cast presence, knowledge state and required outcome
Appendix B chronology/date state where applicable
Implementation/disposition record for meaningful extracted details
story_source_execution_contract.no_silent_omission_rule: Every meaningful source-backed detail discovered during chapter review must be implemented or receive an explicit disposition and reason.
story_source_execution_contract.no_story_shortcut_rule: Do not shorten or skip journey/story detail merely to connect major film anchors. Performance pressure changes streaming/residency strategy, not source coverage.
story_source_execution_contract.gate_rule: Gate 6/7 controls when runtime scope opens; it does not authorize narrative compression or deletion from the source plan.
story_source_execution_contract.dialogue_rule: Runtime dialogue remains original and non-verbatim while preserving source-grounded intent, relationships and knowledge boundaries.
story_source_execution_contract.conflict_rule: Film/screenplay continuity controls film-driven outcomes; incompatible book-only differences are explicitly tagged rather than silently substituted.

localization_contract.voice: English original VO; Arabic dubbing is not required.
localization_contract.map_rule: Canonical Middle-earth place labels on the map remain in their original English names (for example Hobbiton, Bree, Rivendell, Moria, Lothlorien, Minas Tirith). Arabic UI/objective text may refer to those labels without replacing the map label itself.
localization_contract.rtl_rule: Arabic UI/subtitles must use proper RTL layout, shaping, wrapping and fonts that render correctly in UE4.27.2.
localization_contract.subtitle_rule: Arabic subtitles must remain synchronized with English VO and preserve speaker/story meaning and knowledge limits.
localization_contract.quality_rule: Localization QA covers truncation, RTL ordering, line wrapping, subtitle timing/readability, objective clarity and preservation of canonical English map labels.
localization_contract.authority_rule: Localization must not alter canon, locked outcomes, character knowledge or objective meaning.
localization_contract.evidence_boundary: This contract is governance/design truth. It does not claim the runtime localization pipeline is already fully implemented or device-tested.

deep_audit_v1_2026_10_01.key_compound_risk: Settlement entry can align streaming/residency changes, NPC activation, AI/animation/collision, first-use rendering and cleanup work in the same frame window.
useful_existing_mitigations: UShireChapterAssetStreamingSubsystem uses soft object paths and FStreamableManager async loading with resident/pending ownership.
LivingWorldDirector has bounded pooling paths for ambient NPCs, interactions and ambient motion.
WholeGamePooledPopulationPlanV1 defines activation bands and forbids uncontrolled Spawn/Destroy bursts.
WholeGameStreamingResidencyPlanV1 forbids synchronous heavy runtime loading and bounds active working sets.
P1C01HTargetDeviceProfilingPlanV1 already targets DX11 / 720p / 30 FPS / ~2 GB VRAM.
P1C01SaveLoadLongSessionV1 already bounds save payload growth and restore mutation.
required_followup: Measure cold and warm traversal separately.
Capture Game/Draw/GPU frame time plus p95/p99/max tails.
Measure streaming/VRAM pressure on representative target hardware.
Measure NPC activation tiers, pooled counts and activation bursts.
Exercise long-session revisit and repeated Save/Load stability.
Profile first-use rendering/PSO behavior on the chosen target RHI.
deep_audit_v1_2026_10_01.truth_boundary: The audit is a pre-mortem and validation plan. Its ten risks remain hypotheses until current-source or runtime evidence proves a concrete defect.

lead_engineering_operating_policy_2026_1.owner_intent: The project must be led as a professional game-production program: maximum practical quality, continuous delivery, fast visible progress, root-cause problem solving, aggressive use of high-quality licensed/open resources, and durable repository memory so changing programmers do not change the method.
lead_engineering_operating_policy_2026_1.lead_role: The Lead Game Architect is expected to make routine engineering/production decisions autonomously inside canon, provenance, architecture, performance, gate and evidence constraints. Do not stop production to ask the owner for ordinary technical choices that can be resolved professionally from evidence.
product_priority: Make the game visibly read as a real Shire experience before broadening later runtime chapters.

Human/skeletal character presentation, natural terrain, landmarks, architecture, vegetation, materials, lighting and readable route identity outrank backend-only polish unless backend work directly unblocks those visible results.
Prefer large coherent vertical-slice production packets over tiny disconnected increments when safety and reviewability are preserved.
Every major production packet should materially remove a visible proxy/greybox limitation or advance a production human character unless the packet is closing a proven blocker.
blocker_root_cause_loop: Verify the blocker on the live exact head and classify it as source/export, tooling/CI, engine/import, runtime/system, performance, provenance/license, or canon/integration.
Do not repeatedly retry the same exact payload, workflow or workaround after a durable failure reason is known.
Consult project sources/governor first, then official UE4.27/Epic documentation, then mature open-source repositories/issues and experienced developer practice relevant to the exact problem.
For nontrivial blockers, compare multiple viable remedies and choose the highest-quality UE4.27-compatible option that fits the i7 Gen6 / 8 GB RAM / ~2 GB VRAM target.

Separate repairable content/export defects from fundamentally broken assets. Normalize/re-export recoverable FBX content offline when provenance permits; reject irreparable rigs without weakening import/deformation gates.
Record the selected root-cause fix, rejected alternatives, evidence boundary and next production action in repository memory before or with implementation.
After blocker closure, resume visible production immediately; diagnosis alone is not considered delivery.
external_engineering_evidence_order: ProjectGovernor + Project Sources + live develop evidence
Epic/Unreal Engine 4.27 official documentation and engine behavior
Mature open-source implementations and issue histories with reproducible technical evidence
Experienced developer/community practice used as supporting evidence, never as a substitute for project-specific validation
asset_and_content_acquisition_policy: Search broadly for high-quality legal sources when a production asset is missing or rejected; do not behave as if the first available asset family is the only option.
Prefer CC0, permissive/open assets, original/project-authored content and clearly licensed sources with item-level provenance.
Animated production characters must end as skeletal FBX with real skeleton, skin weights and acceptable deformation; OBJ is not a final animated-character format.
Production textures use PNG/TGA and channel-packed masks where appropriate; uncompressed BMP is not accepted for production materials.
Candidate factories should inventory/rank multiple exact payloads cheaply before expensive UE4 runner use and preserve exact hashes to prevent wasteful retries.
A technically clean generic humanoid may be used as a rig/deformation base before final likeness work; technical pass is not visual acceptance.
performance_and_architecture_quality_bar: Heavy runtime assets remain soft-referenced and asynchronously loaded through FStreamableManager/RequestAsyncLoad.
Repeated static world detail prefers HISM/ISM, culling and bounded collision instead of actor-per-prop density.
Ambient NPC scale uses pooling; no high-frequency Spawn/Destroy churn.
No UE5-only dependency, Nanite, MetaHuman Crowd or UE5 PCG migration is allowed as a shortcut.
Quality improvements must be measured against the fixed DX11 720p 30 FPS floor and low-memory target rather than assumed safe from desktop-class examples.
production_batching_and_ci_policy: Batch related implementation into coherent production packets and avoid unnecessary micro-commits that create superseded CI churn.
Use cheap hosted/static filters before the single expensive UE4 self-hosted lane whenever possible.
Do not weaken gates to make the dashboard green; distinguish expected asset rejection from pipeline regression.
Prefer one exact-head validation cycle per stable packet; superseded runs may be cancelled, but repeated cancellation caused by avoidable commit churn is a process defect to reduce.
After merge, delete the temporary branch unless it contains explicitly recorded unique unsalvaged work.
continuity_contract: This policy is repository authority, not chat memory.
Any replacement programmer/agent must read this policy before meaningful production work.

A new worker may improve implementation details but may not silently lower the visible-quality target, narrow source discovery, weaken technical gates, reopen rejected exact payloads or revert to backend-first delivery.
When a better proven method is discovered, update the Governor with evidence and supersede the old method explicitly rather than drifting informally.
lead_engineering_operating_policy_2026_1.evidence_claim_boundary: COMPILE/STATIC/UE4 machine evidence never implies PIE-TESTED, DEVICE-TESTED, VISUALLY-ACCEPTED or FPS acceptance without chapter-specific proof.

p1c01_total_completion_contract_2026_10_.closure_definition: P1C01 may close only when the Shire experience is complete from all agreed player-facing and technical angles, not merely when its main route or settlement construction works.
required_dimensions: Film-driven causal/story spine and required chapter chronology, cast presence, knowledge limits and outcomes.
All meaningful source-backed Shire details discovered during chapter review are either implemented or explicitly dispositioned; no silent omission.
Exploration content that makes the Shire rewarding to wander without breaking canon or chronology.
Side activities/optional interactions appropriate to the Shire and the approved gameplay bible.
Living-world routines, work, social behavior, reactions, fauna/environment motion and story-state response.
Named NPC continuity and bounded contextual memory where required by the project architecture.
Required landmarks, homes, roads, gardens, farms, river/mill/bridge, woodland transitions and Bucklebury/Ferry read naturally and are traversable.
Hero and required human character presentation, animation, locomotion, deformation and runtime hookup.
Quests, objectives, dialogue, cinematics, audio, return-to-control and chapter pacing.
Traversal, collision, nav/path readability and required encounter reliability.
Save/load continuity and intended world/chapter state restoration.
Performance/streaming/VRAM/NPC activation on the target DX11 720p low-memory profile at the declared 30 FPS floor.
Human visual and pacing acceptance for the exact accepted chapter build.
Localization-safe player-facing text foundation. Full Arabic translation remains governed by the existing whole-game localization contract and is not silently moved earlier.
p1c01_total_completion_contract_2026_10_.fun_rule: The chapter must not be a film checklist only; it must contain canon-safe exploration, optional activity, environmental discovery and lived-in world detail so ordinary play is enjoyable between mandatory story beats.
p1c01_total_completion_contract_2026_10_.completeness_rule: Do not call the chapter 100% complete while any required dimension above is materially open. Scope additions discovered from the supplied sources must be implemented or explicitly rejected/deferred with a recorded canon/production reason.
p1c01_total_completion_contract_2026_10_.next_chapter_rule: P1C02 runtime stays locked until P1C01 is Gate 6/7 accepted under this total-completion contract.
p1c01_total_completion_contract_2026_10_.evidence_boundary: This contract raises the closure bar; it does not itself claim any new acceptance state.

p1c01_full_completeness_contract_2026_10.no_silent_omission_rule: Any meaningful supported chapter detail discovered in Sources 00-11, supplied film material, Tolkien source review or the registered chapter plans must be implemented or receive an explicit documented disposition before P1C01 closure.

p1c01_full_completeness_contract_2026_10.closure_gate: P1C01 closes only when all required dimensions are resolved and Gate 6/7 has chapter-specific evidence. No 'mostly complete' or 'main story complete' shortcut opens P1C02.
p1c01_full_completeness_contract_2026_10.evidence_boundary: This contract defines completeness. It does not itself claim any runtime, device, visual, pacing or performance acceptance.
